bento_pipeline1_prose: This chapter uses Tree-sitter for lossless syntax-tree analysis of the full TypeScript source, automatically extracting core exported symbols, data interfaces and dependency topology, and splitting the complex project hierarchy into a visual knowledge index...
bento_pipeline2_prose: Before diving into the Fiber reconciliation mechanism, the slicing rules of MessageChannel priorities must be clear. When React traverses the WorkInProgress tree during the Render phase, the reconciler automatically prioritizes discrete events to prevent UI jank caused by heavy CPU blocking.
bento_pipeline3_prose: The column follows the Mona-Sans Swiss typography standard, blending a two-column reading grid with interactive data-flow diagrams. While reading, you can click any diagram to see the context-related source location in real time...

bento_exp2_desc: Scheduler MessageChannel scheduling is interrupted by higher-priority tasks when the CPU is blocked.

legal_privacy_sec2_title: 2. What We Explicitly Do Not Collect
legal_privacy_sec2_desc: MCP call logs do not record query content and are not associated with personal identity; LLM usage only records token counts. We never sell personal data.
legal_privacy_sec3_desc: Improving recommendation ranking and content quality, quotas and billing, and security audits. LLM calls are processed via model providers, transmitting only necessary content snippets.
legal_privacy_sec4_desc: Export all your data at any time; delete your account at any time to cascade delete tutorial copies, tokens, telemetry, and reading progress. Revoke GitHub authorization at any time.
legal_privacy_sec5_desc: Telemetry events are rolled and pruned based on admin retention settings; personal data is purged from backups within 30 days of account deletion.
legal_terms_sec1_desc: OpenGits is a platform that automatically converts public GitHub repositories into structured tutorials and provides retrieval services for readers and AI clients. Provided as-is; self-hosted version governed by AGPL-3.0.
legal_terms_sec2_desc: You need a GitHub OAuth identity to use full features. You may not upload infringing, unlawful, or harmful content; abuse quotas; or perform malicious scans. Violating content will be removed, and accounts may be suspended.
legal_terms_sec3_desc: Tutorial content is derived from upstream GitHub repositories, and copyright belongs to original authors. Generated within license boundaries; public tutorials require an identifiable open source license. Public tutorials become shared assets; violating content will be removed by administrators.
legal_terms_sec4_desc: Tutorials are automatically generated by AI pipelines and may contain errors or outdated information. Continuous improvements are made via dual-channel quality scoring, upstream sync alerts, and community reports, but accuracy is not guaranteed. Refer to upstream repository documentation for critical decisions.
legal_terms_sec5_desc: To the maximum extent permitted by law, the platform assumes no liability for direct or indirect losses or data loss.
legal_terms_sec6_desc: Material changes will be communicated via in-app announcements. Continued use constitutes acceptance.

mcp_showcase_llamacpp_analogy: Analogy: Like a building-block baseplate — GGML flattens multi-dimensional tensors in linear memory, using strides to address offsets in microseconds without fragmentation.
mcp_showcase_llamacpp_step: Step 1: Core Tensor Structure & Memory Alignment
mcp_showcase_llamacpp_explanation: ggml_tensor is the bedrock of computation graphs. Storing shapes ne[4], strides nb[4], opcodes, and gradient pointers, it achieves zero-dependency matrix abstractions in pure C.
mcp_showcase_vllm_analogy: Analogy: Like OS virtual memory paging — splitting continuous KV cache into physical blocks allocated on-demand, boosting GPU memory utilization from 20% to 96%.
mcp_showcase_vllm_explanation: BlockSpaceManager maintains the mapping from logical blocks to physical GPU memory blocks for each request. CoW or dynamic allocation triggers when tokens exceed block capacity.
mcp_showcase_vgpu_analogy: Analogy: Like a lightweight hardware adapter — bridging headless cloud environments with WebGPU drivers to dispatch local graphics pipelines across distributed clusters.
mcp_showcase_vgpu_step: Step 1: Virtual Adapter & Command Queue Initialization
mcp_showcase_vgpu_explanation: createVirtualAdapter() intercepts standard WebGPU API calls, serializing shader compilation and render pipelines into compact binary frame streams dispatched via Edge Runtime.
mcp_showcase_gpui_analogy: Analogy: Like a game engine render pipeline — bypassing heavy DOM trees to rasterize component hierarchies into GPU vertex batches at blistering 120 FPS.
mcp_showcase_gpui_step: Step 1: Declarative View Component Assembly & Dispatch
mcp_showcase_gpui_explanation: The Render trait calculates geometry through immutable layout constraint trees, while GPUI's batching engine merges layers in microseconds to exploit multi-core Vulkan/Metal hardware.
mcp_showcase_llamacpp_tip_content: Tensor memory addresses must align to 64-byte cache line boundaries. Misaligned access triggers CPU bus locks, dropping SIMD GEMM throughput by over 40%.
mcp_showcase_vllm_tip_title: Production Tip: Block Size Selection Strategy
mcp_showcase_vllm_tip_content: Short dialogues benefit from block_size=16 to minimize tail fragmentation; long-context RAG prefers block_size=32 to lower scheduler metadata overhead.
mcp_showcase_vgpu_tip_content: Direct VRAM handles cannot be shared across serverless runtimes. Shader bytecode requires sandbox static scanning before execution to block side channels.
mcp_showcase_gpui_sum_title: Four Pillars of GPUI Native Rendering
mcp_showcase_gpui_table_title: GPUI vs Desktop UI Framework Benchmarks
mcp_showcase_gpui_tip_content: Prefer lightweight handles (Entity<T>) in render() over deep cloning. Combine with GPUI change subscriptions to repaint strictly when data changes.
